Package org.apache.juneau.rest.client.mcp.v20260728

Class McpClient

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.rest.client.mcp.AbstractMcpClient
org.apache.juneau.rest.client.mcp.v20260728.McpClient
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable
public final class McpClient extends AbstractMcpClient
Typed 2026-07-28 Model Context Protocol (MCP) client facade.

Extends AbstractMcpClient, adding one typed method per 2026-07-28 JSON-RPC method (see McpMethods). Every method stamps the SEP-2243 params._meta envelope (protocol version, client capabilities, client info, and any supplied trace-context fields), builds the corresponding v2 request bean, wraps it in a JsonRpcRequest with the required Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name headers, delegates to the inherited AbstractMcpClient.send(JsonRpcRequest, Map), and then either returns the result re-marshaled into its typed v2 result bean, or throws an McpException built from the response's error.

An optional McpResponseCache can be supplied via McpClient.Builder.responseCache(McpResponseCache) to serve repeat identical calls from cache instead of the wire, keyed off the method and business params (never the per-call _meta, so a per-request trace-context supplier does not defeat the cache).

A server-initiated request delivered over the duplex event-stream channel is routed through the McpDuplexDispatcher registered via setServerRequestHandler(McpServerRequestHandler).

Beta — API subject to change: This class builds directly on org.apache.juneau.rest.client.mcp, which is itself Beta.

Since:
10.0.0

    • connect

      public static McpClient connect(String endpoint) throws IOException
      Builds a client for endpoint with default settings and performs its one mandatory handshake call, returning a ready-to-use client.

      2026-07-28 has no initialize method - serverDiscover() is this revision's handshake - so unlike v20250618's McpClient, forgetting it is a real footgun: nothing in this class's type system forces a caller to call it before callTool(java.lang.String, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>), listTools(), etc. This is the sanctioned one-expression path for the common case of connecting with default settings; use connect(Builder) to customize the transport, interceptors, or other builder settings first.

      Parameters:
      endpoint - The absolute endpoint URL (e.g. "http://localhost:8080/mcp"). Must not be null.
      Returns:
      A new client that has already completed serverDiscover() exactly once. Never null.
      Throws:
      IOException - If a transport-level or (de)serialization error occurs opening the connection.
      McpException - If the server returned a JSON-RPC error for "server/discover".

    • connect

      public static McpClient connect(McpClient.Builder builder) throws IOException
      Builds a client from a caller-configured builder and performs its one mandatory handshake call, returning a ready-to-use client.

      If serverDiscover() fails, the just-built client is closed before the exception propagates - a caller that only ever sees an exception from connect(...) never ends up owning a client (and its underlying transport resources) it has no reference to.

      Parameters:
      builder - The configured builder to build from. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      A new client that has already completed serverDiscover() exactly once. Never null.
      Throws:
      IOException - If a transport-level or (de)serialization error occurs opening the connection.
      McpException - If the server returned a JSON-RPC error for "server/discover".

      public ServerDiscoverResult serverDiscover() throws IOException
      Sends "server/discover".

      Caches its result, so a subsequent discoveredServer() call (including one following the mandatory discovery connect(Builder) already performs) does not need a repeat round trip.

    • discoveredServer

      public ServerDiscoverResult discoveredServer()
      Returns the ServerDiscoverResult cached from the most recent serverDiscover() call.

      A client built via connect(String)/connect(Builder) already has this populated from the mandatory handshake call, so a caller that only needs the discovery info (server capabilities, supported versions, etc.) does not need to invoke serverDiscover() again just to read it.

      Returns:
      The most recently discovered server info, or null if serverDiscover() has not been called on this client, or the most recent call returned a null result.

      Convenience for callTool(java.lang.String, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>) followed by CallToolResult.firstText().

      Kills the ((TextContent)result.getContent().get(i)).getText() cast-and-scan that a caller who only wants the tool's text result would otherwise repeat at every call site.

    • callRaw

      public Map<String,Object> callRaw(String method, RequestParams<?> params) throws IOException
      Performs a JSON-RPC call using a caller-supplied, fully-populated request bean, returning the raw result payload without deserializing into a specific Result subtype.

      Every convenience method on this class (callTool(java.lang.String, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>), getPrompt(java.lang.String, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>), readResource(java.lang.String), etc.) both builds its own request bean internally and deserializes strictly into one known result type, so none of them can represent a paused input_required response (MCP 2026-07-28 SEP-2322 Multi-Round-Trip Requests) or carry the requestState/inputResponses fields a resume call needs to set. This method exists specifically for MRTR-aware callers that must both populate those fields on the request (e.g. on a CallToolRequest) and branch on the response's resultType themselves, decoding into a typed result only once resultType reads "complete".

      Parameters:
      method - The JSON-RPC method (e.g. McpMethods.TOOLS_CALL).
      params - The fully-populated request bean.
      Returns:
      The raw result as a generic Map, exactly as received over the wire, before any subclass-specific deserialization. Never null on a successful JSON-RPC response.
      Throws:
      IOException - On a transport failure.
      McpException - If the server returns a JSON-RPC error.

    • callToolWithElicitation

      public CallToolResult callToolWithElicitation(String name, Map<String,Object> arguments, McpElicitationHandler handler) throws IOException
      Invokes "tools/call", transparently answering any MCP 2026-07-28 SEP-2322 input_required elicitation pauses via handler until a terminal result is reached, using the default max-rounds bound.

      This is the ergonomic counterpart to hand-driving the resume loop with callRaw(java.lang.String, org.apache.juneau.bean.mcp.v20260728.RequestParams<?>), ElicitationRequests, and ElicitationResponses: it detects each pause, decodes that round's requests, calls handler for the answers, echoes them back with the carried requestState, and repeats until the server returns a non-input_required result, which is decoded into a typed CallToolResult. callRaw(java.lang.String, org.apache.juneau.bean.mcp.v20260728.RequestParams<?>) remains available as the low-level escape hatch.

      Parameters:
      name - The tool name to invoke.
      arguments - The tool arguments. Can be null (sent as an empty object).
      handler - The elicitation answer callback, invoked once per pause. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      The terminal call-tool result. Never null on success unless the server returns a null result.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If handler is null, or handler returns a null result or a result map containing a null value for a requested id.
      IOException - If a transport-level or (de)serialization error occurs, or handler throws it.
      McpException - If the server returned a JSON-RPC error.
      McpElicitationLimitException - If the server keeps pausing past DEFAULT_MAX_ELICITATION_ROUNDS.

    • listen

      public McpSubscriptionHandle listen(SubscriptionFilter filter, McpSubscriptionListener listener) throws IOException
      Sends "subscriptions/listen", opening a managed, held-open notification stream on a background thread and dispatching decoded frames to listener until the returned handle is closed, the server completes gracefully, or the connection drops.

      Only the initial "subscriptions/listen" POST (opening the stream) is synchronous — a transport-level failure at that point surfaces here as a thrown IOException. Every frame after that (the mandatory acknowledged frame, zero or more change notifications, and the eventual terminal frame) is decoded on a dedicated background thread and delivered to listener; frame-processing failures surface via McpSubscriptionListener.onError(Throwable), never as a thrown exception from this method. This does not reuse pumpNextServerMessage() (single-shot, closes its stream after at most one event) or McpDuplexDispatcher (request/response-shaped, single registration) — listen(...) needs its own long-lived, multi-frame decode loop.

      Parameters:
      filter - The subscription filter (toolsListChanged/promptsListChanged/resourcesListChanged/resourceSubscriptions). Must not be null.
      listener - The typed callback sink. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      A handle to cancel/close the subscription. Never null.
      Throws:
      IOException - If the initial listen request/stream-open fails.
